messages:
sahil: incident-bot reports spike in `model-serving-5xx` alerts in us-west-2 between 13:24-13:27. lots of noise, paging on rotation. can anyone who’s on call grab initial triage?
incident-bot: [ALERT] model-serving-5xx high error-rate — triggered 13:24:10 — paging oncall@sre — incident id: INC-2026-8491 :rotating_light:
olivia: i’m oncall now, taking it. checking logs + recent deploys. pinging @jamie for infra-level network check.
sahil: thx. steps: check canary instances, load-balancer 5xx patterns, and whether this correlates with the bulk batch job that started at 13:20.
jamie: looking at infra — no recent LB config changes. saw a latency burst on the backend NAT gateway, intermittent 504s earlier but not sustained. forwarding VPC flow logs to thread.
maria: I see correlated increase in KV cache misses for model shard 7 around 13:25. that could amplify upstream latencies causing timeouts and 5xx.
olivia: good find. can we reduce paging noise? right now PD is paging for every aggregated 5xx threshold > 2% in 1m. that’s hurting signal. proposing we change the incident severity mapping to only page for >5% sustained over 3m, otherwise create ticket to eng-sre channel.
sahil: agree on separating page vs ticket. current policy pages on short spikes; lots of false-positives. but need to preserve high-severity pages for customer-impacting regressions.
jamie: re: mitigation, adding short-term fallback: update routing to divert 20% of traffic to model-serving-stable pool (older model variant) until we fix cache misses. this reduces pressure on hot shards. I can flip weights via the router in ~5m.
olivia: please do that and post the command you used. also create a dashboard panel for shard miss rate and per-shard tail latency so we can monitor after the roll.
maria: on alert tuning, suggested new alert rule (draft):
```
alert: model_shard_miss_rate_sustained
expr: avg_over_time(kv_cache_miss_rate{shard!=""}[3m]) > 0.07
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: ticket
annotations:
  summary: "Shard {{ $labels.shard }} sustained cache miss rate >7% (3m)"
```
this makes sure we don’t page on tiny blips and ties severity to ticket not page.
sahil: love this. add a companion page-only rule for overall service 5xx > 5% over 3m with customer-impact label. keep paging minimal.
jamie: router change done: `routerctl set-weight model-serving-stable=0.2 --target=us-west-2` — diverted 20%. seeing immediate drop in CPU and queue times on shard 7.
olivia: can everyone confirm they see improvement?
maria: metrics look cleaner, miss rate down ~40% in the last 2m. 5xx rate falling too.
incident-bot: [UPDATE] INC-2026-8491 — mitigation applied by jamie — traffic diversion active. continue monitoring.
escalations-bot: Note: Per new proposal, alerts labeled `severity:ticket` will not page, will create a ticket and post to #eng-sre only.
sahil: next steps: 1) adopt maria's alert rule + jamie’s page rule in staging, 2) add per-shard panels to the ops dashboard, 3) update routing mapping doc (docs/alert-routing.md) to reflect page vs ticket thresholds and channel mappings, 4) run a small post-incident review at 1600 today. owners: maria, jamie, olivia.
olivia: I’ll open a short ticket to track the dashboard and alert PRs and assign owners. ticket: SRE-5872. adding checklist in ticket: dashboard, prometheus rule, PD policy change, docs update, postmortem note.
maria: I’ll draft the Prometheus PR and include example metrics + test vectors. will also add unit test to ensure alert doesn’t fire on synthetic 2% spikes.
jamie: I’ll update router runbooks and add `routerctl` snippet to the docs. also will prepare an automated rollback hook in case diversion causes regressions.
escalations-bot: Reminder: must run PD policy change as staged rollout — update in PD namespace `redwood-sre` then 15m canary before global switch.
sahil: olive branch: we also should add a low-noise summary channel mapping: critical pages -> #pager-sre, degraded-but-not-critical -> #eng-sre (tickets), info -> #sre-ops. that will reduce cross-team noise.
olivia: agree. also add a tag `customer-impact:true/false` in alerts so oncall knows which ones require customer comms.
maria: logging note: filter repeated benign stack traces from alerts; they clutter the timeline. will add a small regex filter in the alert annotations.
jamie: quick comms — notified support of potential SLA blips, told them we diverted traffic and are rolling updates. no broad customer-facing incident declared yet.
olivia: i’ll do a short handoff to the oncoming oncall at 13:40 with the current state and actions. please add any lingering tasks to SRE-5872.
sahil: thanks y’all. follow-up items for the post-incident: retro on PD thresholds, verify canary rollback behavior, run load test to reproduce the shard miss amplification.
olivia: handoff note -> oncall: @maria will be primary for alerts and PRs, @jamie for router/runbook, @sahil for escalation and final sign-off.
maria: ack.
jamie: ack.
incident-bot: [RESOLVE] INC-2026-8491 — incident marked mitigated at 13:38:00 — monitoring for recurrence for 1h.
olivia: closing thread here for now. will post the PR links to SRE-5872 when created. thanks. :thumbsup:
